app.disclaimer_short: Community tool. Not affiliated with Docker, GitHub, Huawei Cloud or Alibaba Cloud.
app.name: MirrorPilot
app.tagline: Find the fastest mirror for your Docker images
config.containerd_body: For containerd 1.7 and later, which reads mirrors from a file per registry rather than from a table inside its own config. Older releases used the mirrors table, which the panel does not generate: a fragment that has to be merged by hand is a worse answer than saying so.
config.daemon_body: Docker Engine and Docker Desktop. Replaces registry-mirrors outright; merges insecure-registries instead of replacing it, because a plain-HTTP mirror of your own is not ours to remove.
config.empty: No enabled mirror proxies Docker Hub, so there is nothing to generate from. Turn one on, or add one, on the Mirrors page.
config.error.existing: That is not a daemon.json this panel can merge into. Look for a comment or a trailing comma — Docker rejects both, and so does this.
config.error.no_mirrors: There is nothing to generate from. Enable at least one mirror that proxies Docker Hub.
config.excluded_hint: %d enabled mirror(s) were left out: registry-mirrors covers Docker Hub and nothing else, so a mirror proxying something else would sit in the file looking useful while doing nothing at all.
config.existing_hint: Everything it contains that this panel does not manage is carried through unchanged, so the result can be pasted over your own file without a manual diff first. Comments and trailing commas are refused rather than silently dropped.
config.existing_placeholder: Paste your existing /etc/docker/daemon.json here to have it merged
config.mirrors_note: Docker asks these in order and stops at the first one that answers, so the order is the whole value of the list: a fast mirror placed second is a slow mirror. Ranking is by the newest measured throughput, with never-measured mirrors last.
config.mirrors_title: Mirrors, in the order they will be tried
config.relay_body: A relay is not a mirror, and the difference is the shape of the address. A mirror is configured in daemon.json and receives the registry protocol at the same paths as the upstream. A relay takes the whole original address as a path — you ask it for docker.io/library/alpine and it decides where to fetch from. These are the upstreams the panel recognises:
config.relay.error.endpoint: The relay address on file is not usable. Set it again above.
config.relay.error.image: That is not an image address Docker would accept.
config.relay.error.no_endpoint: Set the relay address first: an image reference can only become a pull command once there is something to put in front of it.
config.relay_endpoint_hint: A host, optionally with a path prefix. No scheme: this value goes in front of an image reference, and a scheme there is a syntax error rather than a preference.
config.relay_image_hint: Anything Docker accepts. Docker Hub's implicit library/ namespace is spelled out, because a relay needs the address it would actually fetch.
config.subtitle: What to put on the machine that pulls images, generated from the mirrors you have measured.
config.title: Configuration
config.warn.duplicated: points at a host already listed, so it costs a round trip and buys nothing
config.warn.insecure: is reachable only over plain HTTP, which cannot detect tampering
config.warn.unmeasured: has never been measured, so it goes in on the strength of nothing
dashboard.mirrors_note: A mirror has to be switched on before a batch run covers it. Any single mirror can always be measured by hand.
dashboard.subtitle: Where things stand right now.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
disclaimer.body: MirrorPilot is a free community project. It does not run mirrors of its own and it does not proxy image traffic. It measures sources that others operate, and helps you copy images into a registry you control.
disclaimer.no_warranty: Provided as is, with no warranty. See the licence for details.
disclaimer.official_only: Third-party mirrors are convenient, not authoritative. Check a digest against the official registry when it matters.
disclaimer.title: Before you rely on this
error.already_setup: This panel has already been set up.
error.internal: MirrorPilot hit an internal error. The logs have the details.
error.invalid_credentials: That username or password is not right.
error.locked: The panel is locked. Unlock it first.
error.not_setup: This panel has not been set up yet.
error.password_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
error.session_expired: Your session expired. Please log in again.
error.title: Something went wrong
login.subtitle: Enter your password to continue.
login.title: Log in
password.changed: Password changed. Please log in again.
password.subtitle: Everything encrypted under the old password is re-encrypted under the new one.
password.title: Change password
password.warning: The new password re-encrypts every stored credential. If you forget it, those credentials are gone for good.
probe.egress_body: These measurements are taken from this panel's own network egress — the machine or container it runs in. That is the path a docker pull on this host would take, and it says nothing about any other network.
probe.egress_direct: No proxy variables are set, so the probe connects directly. A pull from another machine, another city or another provider can rank these mirrors very differently.
probe.egress_proxied: This process has a proxy configured, so the probe goes through it. What gets measured is the proxy's path to each mirror as much as the mirror itself.
probe.error.target: The image to measure is not usable. Check the repository and reference in Settings.
probe.error.unavailable: This build has no probe engine wired up, so mirrors cannot be measured here.
probe.limits_body: What these numbers do and do not tell you:
probe.limits_cache: A tag can be answered from a mirror's own cache. Two mirrors measured in the same batch may not have served identical bytes — the resolved digest column is what tells you.
probe.limits_daemon_json: A mirror in registry-mirrors only ever covers Docker Hub. It does nothing for ghcr.io, quay.io, gcr.io or mcr.microsoft.com, which people routinely assume otherwise about.
probe.limits_egress: The vantage point is this host only. A mirror that wins here can lose from somewhere else.
probe.limits_rate_limit: Rate limiting is reported as its own result rather than as a failure. A 429 says the mirror would not talk to us right now; it does not say the mirror is broken.
probe.results_note: One row per mirror, newest measurement each. A dash means the step produced no number — either it never ran, or it finished faster than this host's clock could resolve. That is not the same as zero.
probe.run_all_hint: Runs one after another with a few in flight. A few seconds per mirror; a slow or unreachable one takes up to fifteen seconds.
probe.subtitle: Measure how each mirror actually performs from this machine.
probe.target_note: Every mirror is asked for the same image. A digest is a better choice than a tag: a tag can be answered from a stale cache, which makes the comparison quietly unfair.
probe.title: Speed test
settings.probe_hint: Every mirror is asked for this image. Leave a field blank to use the default shown in grey.
settings.probe_reference_hint: A digest, if you have one, makes runs comparable: a tag may be answered from a mirror's cache and be a different image on two mirrors.
settings.subtitle: Language, appearance, and the image mirrors are measured against.
settings.title: Settings
setup.explainer: The password has two jobs. It logs you in, and it derives the key that encrypts the GitHub and registry credentials you store later. Neither is written to disk.
setup.password_hint: At least %d characters. It also encrypts the credentials you save here, so if you lose it they cannot be recovered.
setup.subtitle: Choose the password that protects this panel.
setup.title: Set up MirrorPilot
sources.delete_confirm: Delete this mirror? Its measurement history goes with it.
sources.enabled_hint: "In use" decides what a batch run covers. Measuring one mirror by hand always works, whether or not it is switched on.
sources.error.builtin_readonly: That mirror ships with the binary. You can turn it off, but not edit or delete it — otherwise the trust badge next to it would mean nothing.
sources.error.duplicate_id: That identifier is already taken. Pick another.
sources.field.enabled: Use this mirror in batch runs
sources.field.id_hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It is the key everything else is stored under, so it cannot change later.
sources.field.insecure: This mirror is only reachable over plain HTTP
sources.field.insecure_hint: Plain HTTP cannot detect tampering. Such mirrors are listed so they can be measured, and are never a good default.
sources.field.name: Name
sources.field.provider_hint: Who runs it. A fact about them, not a rating of the mirror.
sources.field.scope_hint: A mirror only helps for the registries it actually mirrors. One that proxies ghcr.io does nothing for a Docker Hub pull.
sources.field.trust_hint: How much is published about the operator — not how fast or how reliable the mirror is.
sources.field.url_hint: The registry endpoint, with no path. This is the value that would go in registry-mirrors.
sources.id_immutable: The identifier cannot change: your settings and this mirror's measurement history are keyed on it.
sources.subtitle: The mirrors this panel measures, including any you add yourself.
sources.title: Mirrors
sources.trust_body: The trust grade records how much is publicly known about whoever runs a mirror. It is a statement about transparency — not a security guarantee, and not a speed rating.
sources.trust_no_guarantee: Third-party mirrors are convenient, not authoritative. Check a digest against the official registry when it matters.
sync.credentials_hint: Encrypted under the panel's master password and never shown again. Both are repository secrets in the workflow, so the values that can write to your registry never appear in a run log.
sync.dispatched: Run dispatched. GitHub takes a moment to queue it.
sync.dispatch_body: This asks GitHub to run the workflow. The API accepts the request and says nothing else, so whether the copy worked is answered by the run list below rather than by this button.
sync.dispatch_hint: Fully qualified addresses, one per line. A trailing newline is fine; a comma-separated list is not.
sync.error.forbidden: That token is not allowed to dispatch this workflow. It needs the workflow scope on the repository.
sync.error.images: There is nothing to copy. Give at least one image address.
sync.error.no_runs: No runs yet. A workflow that has never been dispatched has nothing to show.
sync.error.not_found: GitHub does not know that repository or workflow. Check the owner, the repository name and the workflow file name.
sync.error.rate_limited: GitHub's rate limit is spent. Wait, then try again.
sync.error.spec: The repository is not set up properly. An owner and a repository are both needed, or both blank.
sync.error.target: The target registry is not set up properly. A registry host and a namespace are both needed, or both blank.
sync.error.token: No GitHub token is usable. Store one below, or check that the stored one has not been revoked.
sync.field.namespace_hint: The path below the registry. The upstream host is dropped, so docker.io/library/alpine:3.21 lands as <namespace>/library/alpine:3.21.
sync.field.ref_hint: Left blank, GitHub uses the repository's default branch. The panel cannot see which one that is.
sync.locked: The panel is locked, so credentials cannot be written. Unlock it first — the key that encrypts them is not on disk.
sync.not_configured: Not ready to dispatch. The repository, the target registry and a GitHub token all have to be set, and the panel has to be unlocked.
sync.runs_note: Read from GitHub when you ask for it, not on every page load. A run that has just been queued can take a moment to appear.
sync.subtitle: Copy images into a registry you control, using a GitHub Actions run that can reach the registries this machine cannot.
sync.title: Relocate
sync.workflow_body: Commit this file to the repository below. GitHub's runners can reach registries that the machine running this panel cannot, so the job is a pull, a tag and a push — nothing else.
sync.workflow_secret_password: ACR_PASSWORD — its password or access token.
sync.workflow_secret_username: ACR_USERNAME — the username for your target registry.
unlock.banner: Locked: your stored credentials are unreadable, so scheduled syncing is paused. Unlock to resume it. You will only be asked once per restart.
unlock.subtitle: MirrorPilot restarted and its encryption key is no longer in memory.
unlock.title: Unlock
